params.body:
## What a visitor without a login can see

The image routes outside `auth` take a base64 storage path and serve whatever is at that path, without asking whose file it is or whether it was published:

- `ownvehicle/image/{path}` and `stocklist/image/{path}` (`ImageController::vehicle_image`, disk `vehicles`)
- `website/image/{path}` (`WebsiteController::image`, disk `vehicles`)
- `dealer/image/{path}`, `dealer_backgrounds/image/{path}` (disks `dealers`, `background_images`)
- `simple/image/{path}` (`ImageController::simple_image`, disk `default`, the bucket root; an SVG is returned as `image/svg+xml` from our origin)

Vehicle photos live at `{vehicle_id}/car_image_{n}.{ext}` (`ProcessVehiclePhoto`), with `thumb_`, `medium_` and `trans_` variants, and vehicle ids are a counter. So the photos of every vehicle on the platform can be listed by hand, including drafts, cars that were never on a website, merchant and export cars, damage photos, and the original of a photo whose published version was blurred.

Checked on production on 2026-11-26: `base64("24173/car_image_1.jpg")` and `base64("24000/car_image_1.jpg")` both answer 200 with the photo, without a session.

## Fix (needs a decision)

Either sign the image URLs (`VehicleImageService::urlVoor()` already builds signed bucket URLs for derived sizes; the proxy routes could take a signature the same way), or, for a guest, serve a vehicle photo only when the vehicle is in a public selection (website, showroom, public API) and only the blurred variant where one exists. `simple/image` should be limited to the folder the simple settings write to. The signed route is the smaller change and covers all of them at once.
params.title: Image routes serve any storage path to a visitor without a login
